lines.trans: Buzz-buzz on a quiet Sunday—that double ring is definitely Room Four.
Right on cue! Look who is coming down the stairs with a green book!
I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
If Room Four ever rang only once, madam, I would think it was broken.
Here is the cloth-bound garden herb book from the second-hand bookshop shelf on Jasmine Street!
Look at the gold leaf stamped on the faded green cover: Courtyard Herbs and Blossoms.
Check inside the front cover first—old neighbours always wrote their street number there.
Good eye, Mazen! Pencilled in the corner is our exact house number from thirty years ago!
This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
Turn the pages gently over the desk blotter so nothing dry slips onto the floor.
Wait—the book falls open all by itself near chapter seven on summer mint!
Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.

examples.trans: He wrote all the street notes in the notebook.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: The word 'لـ' (لـ) means 'لـ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is لـ.

meanings.note: The word 'رامي' (رامي) means 'رامي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is رامي.

meanings.note: The word 'وعمته' (وعمته) means 'وعمته'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is وعمته.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: The word 'اقلبوا' (اقلبوا) means 'اقلبوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقلبوا الصفحات شوي شوي فوق نشافة المكتب عشان ما يوقع إشي ناشف عالأرض.
examples.trans: Turn the pages gently over the desk blotter so nothing dry slips onto the floor.
This is اقلبوا.

شوي.gloss: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)

meanings.en: a little; a moment (شوي شوي slowly)
meanings.note: Means 'a bit / a moment' (استنوا شوي 'wait a moment'); doubled شوي شوي means 'slowly, gently'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناشفة, plural: ناشفين).

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: The word 'عالأرض' (عالأرض) means 'عالأرض'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اقلبوا الصفحات شوي شوي فوق نشافة المكتب عشان ما يوقع إشي ناشف عالأرض.
examples.trans: Turn the pages gently over the desk blotter so nothing dry slips onto the floor.
This is عالأرض.

meanings.note: The word 'استنوا—الكتاب' (استنوا—الكتاب) means 'استنوا—الكتاب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—الكتاب عم يفتح لحاله قريب من الفصل السابع عن نعناع الصيف!
examples.trans: Wait—the book falls open all by itself near chapter seven on summer mint!
This is استنوا—الكتاب.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: The word 'ناخده' (ناخده) means 'ناخده'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'someone / anyone'; with ما في (ما في حدا) it means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.
